text:
anya: starting staged rollout redwood/v2.4.0-canary -> eu-central at 3% for 8m. changewindow 02:30-03:30 UTC. please watch p50/p95 and 5xx.
DeployBot: rollout kicked by anya: redwood/v2.4.0-canary fraction=3% region=eu-central window=8m
eric: noted. are we pinning model variant or letting auto-fallback handle it?
rachel: pinning this canary to avoid silent kernel fallbacks. /deploy pin redwood/v2.4.0-canary@eu-central
aj: QA ran long-sequence prompt set, all green locally. still, watch memory footprints on inf1 nodes.
infra-bot: alert subscription created: eu-central memory-pressure and 5xx spikes. thresholds: mem usage >85% or 5xx >0.6%
DeployBot: traffic routed: 3% -> health checks OK @ t+90s
eric: seeing a smattering of 502s hitting edge-b, small tail lat increase on batchers. not yet at alert.
anya: hold on if 5xx >0.6% or mem >85%. keep logs here.
DeployBot: health event: eu-central: mem pressure detected on pod/model-server-7fc9 -> 92% for 30s. auto-pause engaged, traffic -> 0%
aj: paused. can someone fetch the model-server logs? `kubectl -n inference logs model-server-7fc9 --since=5m`
rachel: tailing logs now. seeing repeated "RuntimeError: tokenizer buffer allocation failed" and then oom-kill. looks like a single worker requesting seq=4096.
eric: that sequence shouldn't be in prod prompt set. maybe a customer spike. still, needs mitigation. options: rollback canary, reduce max-seq enforcement at gateway, or bump instance memory class.
anya: quick vote? my preference: rollback canary to avoid impacting warmup and runbook. low risk.
aj: +1 rollback. pin remains but rollback variant to last known stable and then reintroduce with seq guard.
rachel: prepping rollback. also opening a ticket to add a preflight hook to simulate long-seq requests during canary.
DeployBot: rollback command received from rachel: revert redwood/v2.4.0-canary -> redwood/v2.3.9-stable
infra-bot: scaling suggestion: while rollback runs, consider a short-term firewall rule to block requests with header X-Seq-Length>2048. not ideal but buys time.
eric: can we instead throttle by token-length at edge? i can push a quick lua filter: `if tonumber(ngx.var.http_x_seq_length or 0) > 2048 then ngx.exit(413) end`
anya: do that only if rollback shows continued regressions. for now proceed rollback and keep traffic at 0%.
DeployBot: rollback completed. traffic steady at 0% during operation, then restored to baseline.
aj: verified model-server pods restarted with stable image, no OOMs after 5m.
rachel: releasing post-rollback notes: change-log entry + added follow-up task: add seq-length gate in API gateway and a CI canary script that replays long-tail prompts.
eric: follow-up: create a small canary variant on larger memory class to validate quant/seq combos before changing defaults.
anya: decision log: rollback instead of hotfix. action items: (1) add seq gate on gateway (2) CI canary replay (3) run larger-memory canary for v2.4.0. assign owners in ticket thread. thanks all.
DeployBot: thread closed by anya.
